MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Medical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Sex: Male
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
Targeted genetic testing requested to determine inheritance of maternal COL4A3 variant. Mother is heterozygous carrier of likely pathogenic COL4A3 c.1133G>A p.(Gly378Glu) variant. Clinical concern for possible Alport syndrome in this pediatric patient.

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Male child of mother with known COL4A3 variant. Family history significant for maternal heterozygous likely pathogenic COL4A3 c.1133G>A p.(Gly378Glu) variant. Testing performed to establish inheritance pattern and inform clinical management.

METHOD
Targeted DNA sequencing was performed for the specific familial COL4A3 variant. Genomic DNA was extracted from peripheral blood leukocytes using standard protocols. PCR amplification of COL4A3 exon 18 was performed using gene-specific primers. Bidirectional Sanger sequencing was conducted on ABI 3730xl DNA Analyzer. The reference sequence used was NM_000091.5 (COL4A3).

Minimum coverage depth: >30x
Quality score: Q30 >95%

RESULTS
COL4A3 (NM_000091.5): c.1133G>A p.(Gly378Glu)
Result: NOT DETECTED

The familial likely pathogenic variant COL4A3 c.1133G>A p.(Gly378Glu) was not identified in this patient. Wild-type sequence confirmed at position c.1133.

SUMMARY
Targeted sequencing analysis did not detect the maternal likely pathogenic COL4A3 c.1133G>A p.(Gly378Glu) variant in this patient. This result indicates that the patient did not inherit the familial variant from his mother.

It is important to note that this targeted test only assessed for the specific familial variant. Other pathogenic variants in COL4A3, COL4A4, or COL4A5 associated with Alport syndrome have not been evaluated. If clinical features suggestive of Alport syndrome develop, comprehensive genetic testing of all Alport syndrome-associated genes should be considered.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. The patient did not inherit the maternal COL4A3 variant and is not at increased risk for Alport syndrome based on this specific variant.
2. Targeted testing for the familial COL4A3 c.1133G>A p.(Gly378Glu) variant is available for other at-risk family members.
3. Genetic counseling is recommended prior to testing additional family members to discuss inheritance patterns, testing options, and implications of results.
4. If clinical symptoms consistent with Alport syndrome develop, comprehensive genetic testing including full sequencing and deletion/duplication analysis of COL4A3, COL4A4, and COL4A5 genes should be considered.

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location] Medical Genetics Laboratory. It has not been cleared or approved by the FDA. The laboratory is certified under CLIA to perform high-complexity testing.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
